## Tours with a penguin walk on Martillo Island

Off the coast of [Tierra del Fuego](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), travellers can observe penguin colonies in their natural habitat. The [Martillo Island excursion](/argentina/martillo-island/martillo-penguin-walk/) differs from a standard boat trip: its purpose is to land and observe the birds on foot along designated visitor routes. Martillo is known for its Magellanic penguins, and gentoo penguins can also be seen here.

On our tours, the walk can be booked as an **optional excursion** during a stay in Ushuaia. It is therefore important to distinguish the basic Tierra del Fuego itinerary from the separately charged visit to the colony. The island appearing in a list of possibilities does not itself confirm a landing for every traveller.

## Which Ada Tours itineraries offer the excursion?

In the [14-day “Best of Argentina” programme](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), a visit to Martillo Island is offered during the stop in Ushuaia. The journey also includes Buenos Aires, El Calafate, Bariloche and the Iguazu area. A separate price is given for the optional walk.

Another option is the [12-day “Ice, Sun and the End of the World 2027” tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/), combining Argentina and Brazil. Its Ushuaia programme includes a group excursion to Tierra del Fuego National Park, while the visit to the penguin island is offered as an extra.

These itineraries differ in their overall geography, duration and excursion arrangements. Compare not only the opportunity to see penguins but also the number of nights in Ushuaia, transport time and the schedule of onward flights.

## How walking on the island differs from watching from a boat

On a sea excursion, visitors observe the birds from the vessel. With an authorised landing, they can get closer to the colony on shore. The operator's rules nevertheless specify the distance to wildlife, group size and permitted direction of movement.

The aim is to observe without disturbing the birds. Do not approach nests, block paths or attempt to touch penguins. Selling an excursion does not override conservation rules. Access to the island and the possibility of landing depend on the arrangements of the specific operator and conditions on the day.

Other seabirds, including albatrosses, cormorants and petrels, can be found around the island. Their presence in the region does not guarantee that every species will be seen on a particular day.

## Season and weather: when to plan a penguin encounter

Magellanic penguins return to the island for breeding from approximately late September. The colony's composition and the birds' behaviour change from month to month. Check the visiting possibilities against the season of your chosen tour and the area's conservation rules.

Weather in Tierra del Fuego is changeable: wind, waves and navigation conditions may alter the boat portion of the journey. Bring warm layers, a windproof jacket and footwear suitable for wet surfaces. It can be cold on the water even in summer.

According to Estancia Harberton, access to the penguin island is organised by a separate operator; visiting the estancia itself does not replace booking an excursion to the colony. This is another reason to check the **exact ticket type** rather than assume every cruise through the channel includes a landing.

## The optional excursion price on two programmes

On [“Ice, Sun and the End of the World 2027”](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/), the supplement is **300 USD per person** in a group format. That programme separately specifies an approximately 20-minute transfer to the port and roughly 2 hours of navigation.

On [“Best of Argentina”](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), the excursion costs **450 USD per person**. This is the price of an additional service on a different tour. The difference must be respected; one rate should not be applied to both journeys.

Consider the price alongside the precise excursion inclusions, landing rules, group size and required transport. The base tour prices apply to entire itineraries, not just a single penguin encounter.

## Frequently asked questions about Martillo Island penguin tours

### Can I see penguins without landing on the island?

Yes. Boat-based wildlife observation programmes exist, but they differ from a [walk near the colony](/argentina/martillo-island/martillo-penguin-walk/). Confirm whether your chosen tour includes going ashore.

### Is the Martillo Island excursion already included?

On both of our programmes, it can be added for a separate charge.

### How much does the excursion cost?

On the [2027 programme](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/), it costs 300 USD per person in a group. On the [14-day programme](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), it costs 450 USD. These prices belong to different offers.

### Are penguins present all year round?

Viewing depends on the season and excursion availability. Magellanic penguins return to the island around late September; check exact visiting dates before travelling.

### Where does the excursion take place?

On Martillo Island near Ushuaia in Tierra del Fuego. Travellers follow an authorised sea route, and the operator confirms whether landing is possible.

## Three Luján de Cuyo wineries in one day

[Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/) is one of the well-known wine-producing areas of [Mendoza Province](/argentina/place/mendoza/), in the eastern foothills of the Andes. Vineyards and wineries sit against a mountain backdrop. Our private itinerary visits **three estates**: each includes a tour and a tasting, and **lunch at the third winery is included** with mountain views.

This makes a full wine day different from a brief tasting at one stop. During one outing, you can compare how different estates produce and present their wines. Specific winery names are not fixed in the offer, however: they are agreed when booking. We therefore cannot promise a particular brand, wine collection or vintage without further confirmation.

## What three consecutive visits offer

The first winery is a chance to get acquainted with the region's geography and terminology, the next provides a basis for comparison, and lunch at the third concludes the day. This describes a useful way to experience the outing, **not a fixed sequence of educational topics or individual tasting flights**. The exact content of each visit depends on the estates selected.

Luján de Cuyo has a well-developed wine-tourism culture, and many estates provide production tours and tastings. The area is especially associated with Argentine Malbec, although the varieties in a particular tasting are chosen by the winery. Even without specialist knowledge, travellers can compare aromas, structure and ageing methods, and ask about grape origins and production techniques.

If non-alcoholic alternatives, dietary restrictions or a particular tour language matter to you, mention them when arranging the wineries. Special menus and alcohol-free tastings should not be assumed to be included automatically.

## Lunch with views of the Andes: why to allow a full day

Lunch at the third winery is a **confirmed part of the programme**. It provides a natural conclusion to the tastings without needing to find a separate restaurant. The published description confirms lunch and views of the Andes, but does not specify a particular menu, accompanying drinks or seating arrangement. These details are discussed when choosing the winery.

Travel time between estates also matters on a wine itinerary. Even when the stops are in the same district, the day must allow for driving, guided tours, tastings and an unhurried lunch. It is better to organise a substantial day around three agreed visits than add stops without a time buffer.

Guests planning to taste alcohol should arrange appropriate transport and avoid driving themselves afterwards. **A particular transfer service has not been separately confirmed as included in this excursion price**; the route and transport arrangements must be agreed when booking.

## A wine day within a longer journey

The excursion can be a standalone day in Mendoza or part of a multi-country itinerary. For example, on the current [17-day Chile, Argentina and Brazil programme](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/), the three Luján de Cuyo wineries follow a visit to Patagonia and precede the flight to Iguazu. The wine experience provides a natural contrast to the glaciers and other landscapes.

For other regions and styles, explore [food and wine journeys](/interests/food-and-wine/). It is important to distinguish a full winery day with lunch from programmes in which a tasting is just a short stop between other attractions.

## Frequently asked questions about Luján de Cuyo wineries

### How many wineries are included?

Three. Each includes a tour and tasting; lunch is also included at the third.

### Can I choose specific estates in advance?

The selection is agreed when booking. Visiting a particular estate is possible only after its participation and availability are confirmed.

### Is this excursion suitable for wine beginners?

Yes. The format introduces wine production and allows tastings to be compared. Specialist knowledge is not listed as a requirement for our excursion.

### Is lunch included, and is the menu known?

Lunch at the third winery is included. The exact menu and service details are agreed separately.

### Can I drive myself after the tastings?

It is better to arrange transport that does not require driving after consuming alcohol. The specific transfer should be agreed alongside the itinerary.

## Tours of three Luján de Cuyo wineries: tastings and lunch by the Andes

[Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/) is a renowned wine-producing district of Argentina's Mendoza region. Vineyards sit against the Andes, and wine tourism combines introductions to production with tastings. The [Ada Tours three-winery excursion](/argentina/mendoza/argentina-lujan-three-wineries-lunch/) takes a **full day** and includes lunch at the third estate.

This format suits travellers who want to spend much of their day exploring the wine region. It differs from a brief visit to a single winery followed by other city activities. Here the successive visits and lunch form one coherent programme.

## What is included

The excursion covers **three wineries**, introductions to their operations and tastings at each. Lunch overlooking the Andes is planned at the third estate. The winery tours, tastings and lunch form the core of the agreed programme.

Specific estate names are not fixed beforehand: the choice is confirmed when booking. It would therefore be misleading to promise a particular wine brand, restaurant, collection or producer's cellar unless it appears in the confirmed plan.

Luján de Cuyo is famous for Malbec and other grape varieties, and visitor-focused wineries offer different tasting formats. Match the available programmes to the interests of your group: some guests prefer winemaking history, others the differences between grape varieties, and others the culinary experience.

## Which tour dedicates a full day to this?

The winery programme is scheduled for **day twelve** of the [17-day “Chile and Argentina” Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/). That day's route covers Mendoza and the Luján de Cuyo valley. Following the tours and lunch, guests spend the night at Entre Cielos in a Superior Room.

The following day, the journey continues with a flight from Mendoza to Iguazu. This makes the wine day a separate stage before changing regions, rather than a chance to squeeze in another distant excursion.

The Grand Tour covers far more than winemaking: Chile, Patagonia and Iguazu Falls, with the option of private aviation on certain segments. Accordingly, **the total journey price** reflects complex logistics, accommodation and a wide range of experiences, not merely the cost of wine tastings in Luján de Cuyo.

## Why Mendoza is ideal for wine travel

Winegrowing in Mendoza is shaped by the dry climate and irrigation, while the nearby Andes create recognisable landscapes. Luján de Cuyo has numerous wineries, some of which welcome visitors for tours and tastings. Estates differ in their vineyards, production, architecture and approach to presenting wine.

Evaluate the programme by **the content of each visit**, not the number of glasses poured. Three stops in one day enable comparisons but require time for transfers, guided visits and lunch.

For background on the region, see the [Mendoza page](/argentina/place/mendoza/); the wider topic is covered under [food and wine travel](/interests/food-and-wine/).

## Private format, lunch and limitations

We offer this excursion as a private experience. Tastings at three wineries and lunch at the final stop are confirmed. The guide's language, specific wine labels, menu and separate additional services are not fixed in advance and must be agreed.

When planning the wine day, allow for sensible tasting quantities, food and safe travel between estates. Driving after consuming alcohol is unsafe: transport and a sober driver should be arranged beforehand in accordance with the chosen tour's terms.

For larger groups, check each winery's visitor-capacity limits, whether everyone can taste at the same time and how long lunch will take. The sequence of three estates matters on a full-day private outing so that most of the time is not consumed by travel.

## How this differs from a Mendoza city tour

The [Mendoza city tour](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-city-tour/) focuses on plazas, parks and the history of the city and lasts around three hours. The Luján de Cuyo wine day has a different purpose: tastings, winery visits and lunch with views of the Andes.

If you would like to explore both the city and vineyards, plan them for separate parts of the trip. The fact that both experiences have “Mendoza” in their descriptions does not make them interchangeable: their duration and services differ.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Luján de Cuyo wineries

### How many wineries are included?

On the [Ada Tours excursion](/argentina/mendoza/argentina-lujan-three-wineries-lunch/), you visit **three estates**, with a tour and tasting at each.

### Is lunch included?

Yes. Lunch at the third winery with views of the Andes is included. The exact menu depends on the estate agreed.

### Which wineries are visited?

The specific wineries are selected when booking. They should not be replaced by an arbitrary list of popular brands.

### Which tour includes this excursion?

The full wine day takes place on day twelve of the [17-day Grand Tour of Chile and Argentina](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-private-grand-tour-17-days/).

### Can it be combined with a Mendoza city tour?

If sufficient time is available, this can be arranged under a separately agreed schedule. The city tour is not included in the winery excursion itself.

## Excursions in Mendoza: wineries, the city and the road to the Andes

[Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) lies in western Argentina at the foot of the Andes. The region is famous for wineries, while the city has green avenues and parks. A mountain journey towards Aconcagua, however, is a very different experience from a wine-tasting day among vineyards.

In Mendoza, Ada Tours offers [winery visits and tastings](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-wineries-wine-tasting/), a [mountain route to Aconcagua and Puente del Inca](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/), and a [city sightseeing tour](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-city-tour/). There are also separate wine experiences around Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley. Check the precise inclusions and format before booking, as these programmes differ substantially.

## Mendoza wineries: how tastings are organised

The [6-hour winery excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-wineries-wine-tasting/) includes a transfer and guide. Wine tasting is part of the programme, while **lunch is charged separately**. These conditions must not be applied to every wine excursion in the region.

For other formats, consider a [three-winery visit in Luján de Cuyo with lunch](/argentina/mendoza/argentina-lujan-three-wineries-lunch/) or a [tasting in the Uco Valley](/argentina/uco-valley/uco-valley-winery-tasting/). Their names reflect different geography and content; the full list of wines and estates is set out in each individual excursion description.

Mendoza is often associated with Malbec, but its wineries produce a wider selection. When choosing a food-and-wine day, decide whether you are most interested in production methods, comparative tastings or a winery lunch. Such details are best arranged in advance, because estate visits follow their own schedules.

## The route to Aconcagua and Puente del Inca

The [mountain excursion from Mendoza](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/) follows the Mendoza River valley through the Potrerillos and Uspallata areas towards the natural Puente del Inca bridge and an Aconcagua viewpoint.

Our excursion terms are **6 hours, a group format, an English-speaking guide, a transfer and a price of $150 per person**. Meals are not included. A discount may be available for groups of more than 1 person, but no exact amount is specified. These conditions apply to this excursion only.

Aconcagua is South America's highest mountain. The excursion to a viewpoint **is not a summit ascent**, nor does it promise a high-altitude hiking route. Its main attractions are Andean road panoramas, the natural bridge and the mountain drive.

Weather can change rapidly at altitude, and transport restrictions affect access to individual stops. Warm clothing, sun protection and extra time are particularly important on this journey.

## City sightseeing tour

The [Mendoza city tour](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-city-tour/) introduces the city's squares, green streets and architecture. Attractions include Plaza Independencia, Plaza España, the civic centre and the large San Martín Park.

For travellers arriving in Mendoza primarily for winery visits, the city walk can be a convenient addition. It does not replace trips outside the city, however: most vineyards and mountain attractions require separate transport.

## Choosing an excursion

| Main interest | Suitable experience |
|---|---|
| Wine | Winery visits and tastings |
| Andes | Puente del Inca, Aconcagua |
| City | Mendoza sightseeing |
| Full-day gastronomy | Luján de Cuyo, Uco Valley |

If you have only 1 full day, choose your main objective: an in-depth winery excursion and a drive high into the Andes head in different directions. They cannot simply be combined because they appear close together on a map.

For a longer stay, a practical sequence is a day exploring the city's culture, then the wineries and, separately, the mountains. This leaves room for personal interests and relaxation after travelling.

## Preparation and booking considerations

Wine excursions involve alcohol tasting, so you should not plan to drive afterwards. On the mountain road, altitude conditions and tolerance for long drives matter far more. Durations and guide languages vary: an English-speaking guide confirmed for one excursion does not imply the same service throughout the catalogue.

The full [Argentina excursions catalogue](/argentina/excursion/) lets you compare Mendoza with other regions. If Mendoza is part of a longer journey, [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) show the main itineraries, but some standalone excursions may already be included in a specific tour.

## Frequently asked questions about Mendoza excursions

### Is there a tasting excursion with a transfer?

Yes. The [6-hour winery excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-wineries-wine-tasting/) includes transfer, guiding and tastings. Lunch is charged separately.

### How much is the mountain excursion to Aconcagua?

The [standalone programme](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-aconcagua-puente-del-inca-tour/) costs $150 per person. It is a group excursion and does not include meals.

### Can I visit Aconcagua without mountaineering experience?

Travelling to a viewpoint overlooking the summit differs from climbing it. Mountaineering experience is not itself required for the road excursion, although personal health and travel conditions are important.

### Can I explore Mendoza and the wineries in one day?

Whether this is possible depends on the timing of the separate programmes and distances to the estates. For a relaxed winery visit, it is best to allow a dedicated itinerary.

## Mountain route from Mendoza: Puente del Inca and views of Aconcagua

West of [Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/), the road climbs through Andean valleys and towering cliffs. This Ada Tours group excursion lasts **6 hours**, includes a transfer and an English-speaking guide, and **costs $150 per person**. Meals are paid separately.

## Potrerillos and Uspallata

The road from the city follows the Mendoza River valley, with views of the Cordón del Plata range and Potrerillos Reservoir. The route then reaches [Uspallata](/argentina/place/uspallata/), a historic settlement on the road across the Andes. Other landmarks along the route include Picheuta, Polvaredas, Punta de Vacas and Los Penitentes.

These locations reveal how the terrain changes as the road gains altitude. However, **not every point on the itinerary represents an extended stop**: a substantial portion of the 6-hour excursion is spent travelling.

## Puente del Inca

Puente del Inca, the Bridge of the Inca, is a natural rock formation associated with thermal waters and mineral deposits. Its unusual yellow-ochre colour makes it one of the Andes' most recognisable stops. Despite its name, the stone bridge formed naturally; it was not built by the Incas.

Access to geological features is regulated for safety. Observe the bridge and surrounding scenery from designated points, without crossing barriers on your own.

## Aconcagua: a viewpoint, not a summit climb

[Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) is the highest mountain in the Americas, rising above 6,900 metres. This excursion includes a viewpoint towards Cerro Aconcagua. **A summit ascent, multi-day treks and mountaineering permits are not included in this product.**

Even near the road, conditions are alpine: wind, intense sunlight and low temperatures are possible in the same season. Bring closed shoes, warm layers, water and sun protection. The route and access to viewpoints are checked against the weather and current park regulations.

## Price and format

| Condition | Details |
|---|---|
| Duration | 6 hours |
| Format | Group |
| Guide | English-speaking |
| Price | $150 per person |
| Meals | Not included |

A discount may be available for groups of more than 1 person; its amount is agreed separately.

For a contrast with the mountains, choose a separate [Mendoza winery excursion](/argentina/mendoza/mendoza-wineries-wine-tasting/). Wine tasting is not part of this mountain journey. Full itinerary options are available in the [Argentina tours catalogue](/argentina/tour/).

## Frequently asked questions about the route to Aconcagua

### Can I climb Aconcagua as part of this tour?

No. This is a sightseeing programme with views of the summit.

### In which language is the excursion conducted?

The excursion is accompanied by an English-speaking guide.

### Are meals included?

No. Meals are paid separately.
